messages.subject: Read function error
parts:
Hi, 
I am trying to analyze methylation data obtained through BSMAP. However I seem to be running into a roadblock at the first step.
I get an error with read function. Do you have any recommendation to deal with this
> myobj=read(file.list,sample.id=list("ctrl1","test1","test2","test3","ctrl2","ctrl3"),assembly="hg19",treatment=c(0,1,1,1,0,0), header=TRUE, resolution="base",pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=1,start.col=2,end.col=2,coverage.col=6,strand.col=3,freqC.col=5 ))

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : 
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘read’ for signature ‘"character", "list", "character"’

Also, are there any alternatives to coercing the values to an integer, I believe this would be an oversimplification, I was thinking of may be converting it to percents, but I will cross that bridge when I get there.

Thanks,
Varsha

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Read function error
parts:
Hi, 
I resolved that issue, it was the way I had defined file.list that was the problem, thanks anyways. However, I have a new issue now. I believe it's got something to do with the fact that the read function relies on the nature of the first 100 reads to assign interger/character status (wild guess). 

I believe methylKit treats MT (from chr.col=1) as an integer. Here's the command and the error I get. Do you have any suggestions to correct this? I used BSMap v2.73

> myobj=read(files.list,pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE, chr.col=1, start.col=2, end.col=2, coverage.col=6, strand.col=3, freqC.col=5),sample.id=list("ctrl1","test1","test2","test3","ctrl2","ctrl3"),assembly="hg19",treatment=c(0,1,1,1,0,0))

Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines, na.strings, : 
scan() expected 'an integer', got 'MT'

The MT and X and Y do not turn up until the end of the text files. Is there a way to work around this, I tried changing the MT and X and Y to 24,25,26 respectively but since the files are really large, it just takes a lot of time, and I don't want to introduce error through this formatting.

Thanks
Varsha

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Read function error
parts:
An easy way to diagnose the problem is to work with a smaller sample data set.

From what you said, methylKit expected integer at the chromosome column however, it found "MT". This happened because of the beginning lines used for assigning the class of the columns. One way is to convert all the chromosomes into "character" class.  You may try converting all the chromosomes into a format like "chr1,chr2.................or chr_1,chr_2..................". This doesn't let the methylKit expect an integer!

The following codes (use any one) are pretty faster if you work on unix based environment (linux or MAC)

$awk '{print "chr_"$0}' <input_file_path>
$sed 's/^/chr_/g' <input_file_path>


Regards,
Kalyan
